Sorry, I have a hs diplorable, but I love science.

So please let me know why atoms decay.

Well, there are two ways an excited atom can decay: spontaneous and stimulated.

Spontaneous decay happens randomly, but obeys certain statistics. There's no preferred direction for the radiation to go, that's fully random. When it decays depends on how highly excited the atom is (and some symmetry stuff). The higher the energy level, the more unstable the state and the faster it will decay. This is the concept of half-life. You can't predict when a single atom will decay, but if you have enough of them, you can predict when (approximately) half will have decayed.

Stimulated emissions happens when an excited atom is exposed to radiation that matches the frequency of the radiation it would give off when decaying. It will cause the atom to decay faster, and the radiation sent off will perfectly match that of the stimulating radiation. That's the principle of how lasers work. You have a medium whereing most atoms are excited, and you keep bouncing the radiation they give off back and forth between two mirrors. Every new decaying atom adds a new photon to the already coherent radiation, making it brighter and brighter, until you have a bright beam consisting solely of exactly the same kind of radiation, very focused and with one very clearly defined frequency.

There are some theories that say that spontaneous emission is stimulated emission from interacting with vacuum excitations, but I think it's a bit of a stretch. It could be true though.

No, the President isn't a dictator. Here are some examples:

The President doesn't make laws, Congress does. The President can choose not to sign a law, but even then, Congress can override him.

Congress can impeach the President if he does anything illegal. In fact, they've done this several times.

Congress has to approve any treaty the President unilaterally signs.

The Supreme Court decides what laws are unconstitutional, not the President. If the Supreme Court does something the President doesn't like, he has the power to... sit and spin. They're appointed for life.

The States have all powers not explicitly granted to the Federal Government, so if the President wanted to, say, tell a state what it could our could not do with it's local law enforcement agencies, he'd get laughed at.

His power is great, but limited.

So these executive orders are not law?

Executive orders have the full force of law when they take authority from a legislative power which grants its power directly to the Executive by the Constitution, or are made pursuant to Acts of Congress that explicitly delegate to the President some degree of discretionary power (delegated legislation).

Meaning they are law when Congress or the Constitution already said the President can do that. The President can't just make an executive order about anything he wants, and he can't make an executive order giving himself more authority.

In any event, the Supreme Court can strike down any executive order they deem unconstitutional.

The President's power is balanced by the Congress/Senate and the judicial branch. The idea is that each part of the triangle balances the effects of the others.

Note: the president can elect supreme Court judges which does help somewhat but the President is sworn to protect the Constitution.
